newsitem.title: USA: Fred Meyer to acquire Smith's Food.
newsitem.headline: Fred Meyer to acquire Smith's Food.

text.p: Fred Meyer Inc said Monday it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire Smith's Food & Drug Centers Inc in a stock swap valued at about $720 million.
Meyer said it also would assume about $1.3 billion of Smith's debt.

Meyer said it expects the proposed acquisition to be accretive to earnings per share in 1998. Anticipated cost savings, operating efficiences and significant savings from refinancing opportunities in the combined company will improve earnings, it said.
In the aggregate, these benefits are estimated to be about $65 million annually, it said.

The merger will create a multi-regional supermarket and general merchandise retailing company with 265 major stores in 11 states, the companies said. Sales in 1997 will be about $7 billion, they said.
Under the agreement, Smith's shareholders will receive 1.05 shares of Meyer common for each share of Smith's.
Smith's Chief Executive Ronald Burkle is to become chairman of the combined companies, while Meyer Chairman and Chief Executive Robert Miller is to become president and chief executive.
The deal has been approved by the boards of both companies.
